draft.title: Landscapes and landforms
card: A large area of the Earth's surface with its own look. A desert or a coastline is a landscape.
A single natural feature of the land, such as a mountain, valley, dune or headland.
A landscape is made up of many landforms. A coastal landscape may include headlands, beaches and cliffs.
Think of size. A landform is one feature. A landscape is the whole area where many features sit together.
draft.remember: One feature is a landform. Many landforms together make a landscape.

a.q: Which of these is a landform rather than a landscape?
a.why: A dune is one single feature of the land, so it is a landform. The other options name whole areas made of many features, which are landscapes.
a.clue: Which one is a single feature, not a whole area?

b.q: A hiker in Tasmania walks through an area of high peaks, deep valleys and rocky ridges. What is the whole area best called?
b.why: The area is large and contains many features, so it is a landscape. The peaks, valleys and ridges are each single features, so each is a landform, not the whole area.
b.clue: Is the question about the whole area or one feature in it?

problems.detail: Three options share the pattern '... region' and the right answer is the only one without it, so a student could pick it as the odd one out without knowing the idea.
